evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six-armed oxblood star with side arms and clay dots; glyph-like shapes sit at the arm bases but read as blobs, not a legible word. By shot-20s hairline branches fill the lattice around the star.
evidence.ambition: shot-20s: one flat vector layer in two colours with a six-arm lattice, hairline branches and a small bottom-left caption; no lighting, material or simulation is visible.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: clean clay ground with an oxblood star, a consistent two-colour palette and centred symmetry; shot-08s: glyph shapes at the arm bases clump into smudges and hairlines alias at 1280x720.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: rose-clay ground with an oxblood six-arm star, a familiar snowflake motif. shot-20s: the warm rust palette is close to the recent Penrose night, but the subject and lattice arms differ.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: centred, composed star with ample margins. shot-20s: arms fill more of the frame and branches lengthen, so the piece resolves into a fuller figure, though the 2s frame is sparse.

pairwise_justification: Median shot-20s: dense ochre and rust Penrose kite mosaic inside a cream triangle reads as a finished tiled object; tonight shot-20s has thin oxblood hairline branches that lose weight at thumbnail size.

critique.change: Replace the glyph-blob arm bases at shot-08s with the word defect as legible letters, each sitting at a constant lag behind its arm tip, so the fixed-lag birth reads on screen.
Thicken the hairline side branches at shot-20s and add a second tone or subtle shading to them so they hold at thumbnail size and the piece gains some material.
Use the empty clay ground at shot-02s: add a faint depth or texture behind the star, or start the tip closer to the arms, so the opening frame is not sparse.
